issues.problem: Regression from this branch; it reproduces the live incident through a path the f3 fix did not close. After a Velín storno the booking is 'refund_pending'. The new syncRefundBooking (compare-and-set) does not overwrite 'refund_pending', so the booking stays in that state until process-refund writes its own status. If charge.refunded arrives before that (normal Stripe latency of 1–3 s, which is near-certain for multi-payment refunds because the remainder refunds take time), the webhook's safety-net cancellation mail calls send-cancellation-email with refund_amount = charge.amount_refunded. That calls process-refund with an amount, the 'refund_pending' gate lets it through (the fresh-credit-note dedup only runs for 'partial_refund'), and a second real refund is created. Reproduced: a 50 % Velín storno on 1 payment refunds 3000 instead of 1500 (e_wh_test W1). With 3 payments it refunds 1580 instead of 1565 and sends a false staff mail (b_storno_test M1/M2 'during'). With a pending refund: P2, PS1. Deploy window with the new webhook and old process-refund or send-cancellation-email: f_deploy_test X1/X2. The same tests pass on origin/main, because the old webhook wrote the status first.
issues.fix: In the webhook's send-cancellation-email body add `skip_refund: true`. A charge.refunded event means the refund already happened, so the mail should only attach the credit note through the existing 'cancellation_retry' recovery loop. The live send-cancellation-email already honours skip_refund, so this is safe in the deploy window. Validated in the scratch copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vel-n/a6963cc3-5559-53b7-8eeb-5fd2cdb37dae/scratchpad/paydec/vrf/fixtry: W1, M1/M2 during and replay, P2, X1/X2 and G6 pass. Also do the process-refund dedup in the next issue.

issues.problem: Cancellation refunds are not exactly-once. A second dispatch of the same storno refund always arrives, from Velín's send-cancellation-email after its own process-refund call, from the DB trigger, from webhook replays, or from retries. It creates real money when: (a) the first Stripe refund is 'pending' (low Stripe balance). The status stays 'refund_pending', no dedup runs, and the refundable amount has dropped, so the idempotency key differs: a 50 % Velín storno refunds 100 %. P1 fails on branch and on main. (b) The first dispatch was short because a remainder refund failed. The second dispatch treats the amount as additional and retargets to the original payment: 1673 Kč refunded for 1558 Kč due (S1). This fails only on the branch and is caused by the multi-payment retarget. (c) A second dispatch runs between the main refund and the remainder (DB trigger with the same storno-table amount): 3130 Kč refunded for 1565 Kč (h_concurrent_test H1). (d) A charge.refunded replay after the 30-min mail lock and the 15-min credit-note window refunds again (G6, also on main). In the full-storno case, the second dispatch sends a false staff mail 'zbývá 3015 Kč' although everything was refunded (S2, H1 full). Staff following that mail would pay a second time.
issues.fix: Treat reason 'cancellation' as a TARGET total, executed once. (1) Take a lock at the start of every cancellation dispatch, with or without an amount, using the existing live RPC claim_email_send(booking_id, 'refund_cancellation', 2). A dispatch that loses the lock returns {success:true, already_refunded:true, in_progress:true} without calling Stripe. (2) Compute already = Σ Stripe refunds (succeeded or pending) with metadata mg_source='process-refund', mg_reason='cancellation', mg_booking_id=booking across ALL booking PaymentIntents (stored PI, metadata search, history refs, including fully refunded ones; otherRefundableIntents drops those, so a new helper is needed), plus manual cancellation credit notes. Then refund only max(0, amount − already), or return already_refunded. (3) Compute the short-mail figure against the same target. A scratch prototype (~30 lines, fixtry/process-refund/index.ts, amount path only) makes P1, S1, S2, H1 50 %, T1 and T1b pass. Also extend the plain duplicate dedup (same reason and amount within 15 min) to the 'paid'/'refund_pending' states and base it on Stripe refund metadata instead of credit-note totals, which _cap_refund_to_paid can lower.

issues.file: supabase/functions/send-cancellation-email/index.ts (refund_percent == null → storno table, ~263-321) + live DB trigger trg_notify_booking_cancelled_email (notify_booking_cancelled_email, not in repo)
issues.problem: Pre-existing in the code that is live now, on origin/main after hotfix #2213. Every status → 'cancelled' fires pg_net to send-cancellation-email with only booking_id, reason and source, without refund_amount or refund_percent. send-cancellation-email then computes the refund from the storno table (≥7 days 100 %, 2–7 days 50 %, <48 h 0 %) and calls process-refund for real. That dispatch fires at commit, before Velín's own send-cancellation-email, so it wins claim_email_send. Velín's call is then skipped, and the admin's refund choice is overridden. Reproduced with the real handlers on both main and branch: a Velín storno with 50 % chosen (start in 20 days) refunds 3000 Kč, whether the trigger runs alongside or after Velín's process-refund (c_trigger_test T1, T1b). A Velín storno 'bez vratky' (0 Kč) refunds the full 3000 Kč (T2). The customer mail also states the storno-table amount. For QR/Fio bookings it creates a second manual credit note and, with a Fio token, a second Fio payment. For customer cancellations (cancel_booking_tracked) the trigger dispatch ignores _storno_cap_after_move if it wins the claim; T3 passes only because of request ordering. This produces exactly the '50 % storno → 100 %' symptom, so the hotfix may not have removed the live cause.
issues.fix: Edge-only change in send-cancellation-email. When the body has neither refund_amount nor refund_percent (trigger dispatch), never compute the storno-table refund and never call process-refund. Instead: wait about 5–10 s without taking the claim. If claim_email_send(booking, 'booking_cancelled') is then held by the explicit dispatch, skip. Otherwise take refund_amount/percent from the latest booking_cancellations row (cancel_booking_tracked writes it in the same transaction; Velín writes it right after the UPDATE) and send the mail with skip_refund. If there is no row, send the mail without a refund and an ops mail. Optional SQL for the owner: let the trigger skip cancellations that send their own mail. The lock in the previous issue also narrows T1/T1b, but T2 still needs this fix. Fix this in live independently of the payments merge.

issues.problem: Regression from f3. After a pending Stripe refund, payment_status stays 'refund_pending' forever. The webhook no longer overwrites 'refund_pending', and there is no handler for refund.updated or charge.refund.updated; on main, charge.refunded overwrote it (d_more_test PS1 fails on branch, passes on main). Consequences: Velín shows 'Čeká na vrácení' and offers 'Potvrdit vrácení' with the default amount = total_price. Confirming sends process-refund without an amount, which passes the gate and refunds the whole remaining balance (a 50 % storno becomes 100 %). Every later automatic dispatch also passes the gate (P1). On a live booking (Velín BookingModifyModal shortening with a pending refund), the booking keeps 'refund_pending', and a later Velín storno hides the refund picker.
issues.fix: Resolve the pending state. Subscribe the webhook to charge.refund.updated (owner: Stripe dashboard endpoint events). On status succeeded, write the status process-refund would have written without the pending state; on failed, revert and send a staff mail. Store that status in the process-refund debug_log 'stripe_refund_created' response_data (refundedStatus computed with refundStatus 'succeeded'), keyed by refund id. As a fallback in charge.refunded, when the latest refund is 'succeeded', mg_source is 'process-refund' and the booking is 'refund_pending', apply that stored status with a compare-and-set from 'refund_pending'.

issues.problem: Pre-existing, but now fixable with the multi-payment data. A service or admin refund with an amount (web shortening or cheaper-bike RPC via pg_net, Velín BookingModifyModal) that exactly drains the stored PaymentIntent marks a LIVE booking 'refunded'. process-payment stores every app surcharge PI in bookings.stripe_payment_intent_id, so 'extend by a day by card, then shorten by a day' drains it, while the original 3000 Kč is still paid. Later storno: Velín sees wasPaid=false and shows no refund picker. send-cancellation-email calls process-refund, which takes the idempotent 'refunded' branch, so nothing is refunded and no staff mail is sent: the customer loses 3000 Kč (i_live_status_test L2; b_storno_test L1). The no_op branch also writes 'refunded' for live bookings.
issues.fix: In refundedStatus, pass the booking status and the remaining in-price balance after the refund (staffFullBalanceHaleru minus this refund). Return 'refunded' only when the booking is cancelled or completed AND the remaining in-price balance is ≤ 0. Return 'partial_refund' for any live booking with total_price > 0 or remaining balance > 0. Apply the same rule in the effectiveAmountHaleru === 0 no_op branch: never write 'refunded' for a live booking.

issues.problem: Pre-existing semantic mismatch: the Velín modal amount is the TOTAL refund for the storno (it is written to booking_cancellations.refund_amount), but process-refund treats an amount as ADDITIONAL. (a) On a cancelled 'partial_refund' booking (for example after a 50 % storno), 'Potvrdit částečné vrácení' at 100 % sends no amount. process-refund takes the idempotent 'partial_refund' branch and returns success with already_refunded: nothing is refunded. Velín shows success, and the customer mail says 3000 Kč will be refunded while only 1500 Kč was (d_more_test V1, fails on main and branch). (b) An intermediate total such as 2000 Kč refunds 2000 Kč more, capped only by Stripe. (c) If the remaining amount equals an existing credit note, the step is skipped silently. (d) cancelBookingFromVelin treats only 'paid' as paid. A booking already partly refunded by an earlier shortening ('partial_refund') is cancelled with no refund picker, and the trigger's storno table decides.
issues.fix: In confirmCancelledRefund, send the delta: amount = amt − Σ|non-cancelled credit notes since cancelled_at| (or pass target_total and let process-refund compute it, as in the target fix above). If the delta is ≤ 0, skip with a message. Never send 'no amount' for a booking that is not 'refund_pending'. Drop the 'creditNotes.find(=== amt)' skip in favour of the delta. In cancelBookingFromVelin/BookingCancelModal, treat 'partial_refund' as paid with the refundable rest (total_price) and pass refund_amount/percent explicitly.

issues.problem: A full storno from Velín refunds only the Stripe in-price balance. A part of the price paid by QR or bank transfer is silently not refunded. Velín's modify flow asks for surcharges by QR (mod_surcharge_vs), so card booking + QR surcharge is a normal case. Example: total 4000, 3000 by card, 1000 by transfer. Full storno refunds 3000, status becomes 'refunded', there is no credit note or staff mail for the 1000, and the customer mail says 4000 Kč (b_storno_test Q1, also on main). With an explicit amount (customer storno 4000), the short-refund staff mail is sent, so only the no-amount path is silent.
issues.fix: In the full path (no amount, staff or service), also compute the in-price income outside Stripe: fio_transactions by booking_id / payment_vs / mod_surcharge_vs, minus manual credit notes, as in customerManualCapCzk but without subtracting total_price. If it is > 0, issue the manual part as in manualBookingRefund (credit note + tryFioRefund / 'refund_pending' banner), or at least send the existing 'nevrátila celá' staff mail and set 'partial_refund'. The response must not let the mail claim the full amount.

issues.problem: Two credit notes can be issued for one refund (pre-existing, also on main). Webhook recovery (webhook_refund_retry → createCreditNoteForExistingRefund) and the running process-refund each check 'no credit note for this refund id' and then insert. There is no unique index on invoices.stripe_refund_id, so if both checks pass before either insert, both insert. Reproduced: a 1500 Kč refund gets credit notes −1500 and −1500 (d_more_test CN1). _cap_refund_to_paid does not prevent it while DP ≥ sum. Credit notes then exceed refunded money, and the final invoice and accounting are double counted. The reconcile step only raises an existing credit note and never removes a duplicate.
issues.fix: SQL draft for owner approval (feature-detected, idempotent): CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_invoices_credit_note_refund ON invoices(stripe_refund_id) WHERE type='credit_note' AND stripe_refund_id IS NOT NULL AND status <> 'cancelled'. Both inserts treat 23505 as 'already exists': re-select by stripe_refund_id and reconcile. Edge-only fallback: after inserting, re-select credit notes with the same stripe_refund_id. If there are more than one, mark the newer as 'cancelled', together with its accounting entry, and reconcile the survivor.

issues.problem: Webhook recovery never issues a credit note for a booking's SECOND refund. The webhook sends refund_id, but process-refund ignores it. ensureCreditNotePdf returns the booking's latest existing credit note, and createCreditNoteForExistingRefund only uses bookings.stripe_refund_id, which the webhook writes only when it is null. If process-refund dies after refunds.create on a later refund (second shortening, or storno after a shortening), that refund never gets a credit note. Reproduced: 800 Kč refunded, credit notes total 500 Kč (d_more_test R1, also on main).
issues.fix: In the recovery branch, when body.refund_id is set and there is no non-cancelled credit note with stripe_refund_id = refund_id, call createCreditNoteForExistingRefund with that refund id: parametrise the id instead of reading bk.stripe_refund_id, and check that refund.metadata.mg_booking_id matches. Only fall back to ensureCreditNotePdf when there is no refund_id.

result.summary:
The f3 refund code is **not safe to go live**. A 50 % storno from Velín can still refund 100 %, and the code that is live right now (main after hotfix #2213) refunds too much through another path.

**How I tested.** I built an end-to-end harness that runs the real `process-refund`, `webhook-receiver` and `send-cancellation-email` handlers against a fake Stripe (it models pending refunds, idempotency keys and charge.refunded events) and an in-memory DB, including the live DB trigger `trg_notify_booking_cancelled_email`. It has 32 scenarios. The same scenarios also ran against origin/main, against mixed old/new versions (the deploy window), and against a scratch copy with prototype fixes. The repo's own deno tests still pass (133/133). I changed nothing in the repo or the database.

**Results (32 scenarios)**

| Code | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| Branch | 12 | 20 |
| origin/main (live) | 13 | 19 |
| Branch + prototype fixes | 23 | 9 |

**Worst problems**

1. **Branch regression, matches the live incident.** If Stripe's refund event arrives before `process-refund` writes the status, the webhook's backup storno e-mail calls `process-refund` with an amount. The new compare-and-set no longer overwrites `refund_pending`, so a second real refund goes through: a 50 % storno refunds 100 %. With 2–3 card payments this ordering is almost certain. Adding `skip_refund: true` to that webhook call fixes it in my tests.
2. **Already live today.** The DB trigger on cancellation calls `send-cancellation-email` without an amount. It computes the refund from the storno table and wins the e-mail lock before Velín's own call, so the admin's choice is ignored: 50 % chosen gives 100 %, "bez vratky" gives 100 %. This alone produces "50 % storno → 100 %" on the current live code, so the hotfix may not have removed the cause.
3. **Second dispatch of a storno refund is not exactly-once.** A pending Stripe refund (low Stripe balance) gives 100 % for 50 %, on main too. After a failed remainder refund, the next dispatch over-refunds by 115 Kč (branch only). Overlapping dispatches give 3130 Kč for 1565 Kč. A Stripe webhook replay after 30 minutes refunds again. Staff also get false "X Kč not refunded" e-mails. A prototype lock plus "storno amount is a target, subtract what was already refunded" passes these tests.

Other major issues:
- A pending refund now leaves the booking in `refund_pending` forever (regression).
- A live booking is marked `refunded` when a refund empties the stored surcharge payment. A later storno then refunds nothing (the customer loses 3000 Kč).
- Velín "Potvrdit částečné vrácení" at 100 % refunds nothing but reports success, and the customer e-mail promises the full amount.
- A full storno ignores the part paid by QR or bank transfer, with no staff notice.

Minor: two credit notes can be issued for one refund (race with webhook recovery), and recovery never issues a credit note for a booking's second refund.

**What holds:**
- The recovery-only webhook call never creates a refund.
- The new full-storno calculation is correct for card payments, an attached e-shop order, a refunded duplicate payment and a storno after a failed swap.
- Credit notes are corrected to the real amount when a refund is split across payments.
- The compare-and-set keeps `partial_refund`.
- The app's shortening refund across 2 payments works, and a repeated call refunds nothing more.
- Old webhook with new other functions is safe in the deploy window. New webhook with old functions shows problem 1, so the fix belongs in the webhook itself.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vel-n/a6963cc3-5559-53b7-8eeb-5fd2cdb37dae/scratchpad/paydec/vrf:
- README.txt — how to run
- harness.ts
- fakes/
- t/a_smoke_test.ts
- t/b_storno_test.ts
- t/c_trigger_test.ts
- t/d_more_test.ts
- t/e_wh_test.ts
- t/f_deploy_test.ts
- t/g_paths_test.ts
- t/h_concurrent_test.ts
- t/i_live_status_test.ts
- main/ — origin/main copy of the 3 refund functions + _shared
- fixtry/ — prototype fixes

verify:charges (adversarial), against HEAD cab35677. The payment code is unchanged since 1d57d742. I found no blocker and no regression against the pre-merge production 550ad417. All checks pass. I found 1 major issue. It already existed in 550ad417, so it is not a regression, but it is an easy money exploit. I also found 9 minor issues: 3 new, mostly latent; 4 carried over from earlier rounds and still not fixed; 2 that predate this work.

Checks run (no git writes, no live DB writes):
- **Deno tests:** 133/133 pass.
- **Deno check:** error counts equal the baseline: process-payment 98, webhook-receiver 77, payment-flows 87, pp-waiver 51, complete-extension 6, checkout-labels 6. All shared modules, process-refund (index, other-intents, credit-note-sync), refund-recovery and generate-invoice have 0 errors.
- **SQL drafts p1–p4:** applied twice each on 3 fresh DBs built from tmpl on /var/tmp/pg-paydec. The template md5 151de752 equals the current live snapshot df555c93 (2026-10-22 08:35). One DB (vch3) first got main's 20261022_gear_rental.sql and 20261022b_live_viewers.sql. 0 errors on every run, 127/127 tests each time. None of the functions the drafts replace were changed by main's new migrations. My DBs are dropped. The cluster was already running for another agent (DBs vca/vcb), so I left it running.
- **Web node suites:** test_web 49/49, test_guard_paid 25/25, test_f1 29/29, test_guard_f1 29/29. test_fix6 is 35/36; the one failure is the known stale scan.js regex (free_unverified).
- **php -l and node --check:** clean.
- **App payment tests (12 files):** Android 101/101. iOS tar copy (pub get --offline, Android tests copied in) 101/101.
- **flutter analyze:** Android 147 issues, iOS copy 143, 0 errors in both, same as baseline.
- **Trees:** diff -rq of the payment files shows only whitelisted files and v2 seams.
- **Scratch test** /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vel-n/a6963cc3-5559-53b7-8eeb-5fd2cdb37dae/scratchpad/paydec/vc2/t/matrix_test.ts: 5/5 pass. Two results matter:
  - 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 1.01 / 14.49 / 14.5 / 14.99 / 15 / 15.4 / 15.5 / 100 are classified the same by the app and the server. The 4.1.3 matrix holds: charged only what it sends, refused below 15.
  - Attempt-id reuse ignores the amount (issue 3).
- **Cleanup:** the 124 MB iOS copy is deleted.

What held:
- **Rounding and waiver** stay inactive until the SQL is live, on every path (app booking, SOS, shop, extension, swap, gear; web booking, product/gear rental, edit). Each checks for the column or the RPC version first.
- **App 4.1.3** is charged exactly round(amount) via a PaymentIntent. It never reaches the server-priced Checkout path. Below 15 Kč it gets a 400 below_minimum and nothing is charged.
- **Webhook confirmations:**
  - The rounding is written with compare-and-set before confirmation. A replay returns 'already'.
  - A rounding write failure returns 500 before confirm.
  - Duplicate charges are refunded with the deterministic keep-earliest rule.
  - A late payment of a cancelled booking is refunded once.
  - Extension payments no longer revive cancelled bookings.
- **Intent guard:** live → payment_in_progress. Open → reuse only with the same amount, type, chg_hash and due/rounding metadata, otherwise cancel. A failed cancel is re-checked. Fully refunded stored PIs, or partly refunded ones on an unpaid row, no longer block.
- **Documents:** booking/shop/edit lines (including rounding) and Stripe Checkout lines sum to the charge.
- **Deploy window:** safe in both directions:
  - old webhook + new process-refund: the old webhook writes the refund status first, so a call without amount takes the idempotent path;
  - new webhook + old process-refund: the old process-refund already treats a `_retry` reason as recovery-only.
- **Pre-merge behaviour without SQL** is identical except for the intended D1–D6 fixes.

Carried-over open items (f2/f3 minors 4–9 below) were not fixed by fix:f3, which only addressed its 4 refund issues.

issues.problem:
The currency comes from the client on every charge path (`currency: currency || 'czk'` / `body.currency || 'czk'`), and the webhook confirms booking/SOS/shop payments without checking PaymentIntent/session currency. A customer can pay a 3 000 Kč booking as 3 000 HUF/UAH/INR (a fraction of the price). Two ways in:
- the app API with their own JWT (saved card);
- with no login at all, a POST {source:'web', booking_id, currency:'huf'} to the web booking checkout.
confirm_payment marks the booking paid, and financial_events books paymentIntent.amount/100 as CZK. This was already in 550ad417, so it is not a regression. It defeats the server-authoritative amount checks added in D4. No legitimate client needs another currency: the app sends none, web booking/edit send none, gear-rental sends 'czk'.
issues.fix:
Server: ignore body.currency and use the constant 'czk' in every paymentIntents.create, checkout line item and response. Alternatively, refuse 400 invalid_currency when a non-'czk' value is sent.
Webhook (payment_intent.succeeded and checkout.session.completed booking/SOS/shop/extension branches): if (pi.currency || session.currency) !== 'czk', do not confirm. Insert a debug_log 'payment_wrong_currency' row and send the ops mail (optionally auto-refund with an mg_source key, like late_payment).

issues.problem: New D4 path. When confirm_payment cannot revive a cancelled booking ('revive_failed'), refundLatePaymentOnCancelled refunds the WHOLE PaymentIntent with no amount. The handler then still calls confirmShopPayment(metadata.shop_order_id) for the bundled web e-shop order. Result: the shop order (goods/voucher generation, DP) is marked paid although all the money went back. Today this is latent: the web upsell bundle only exists while feature flag reservation_upsell is on (off per D7).
issues.fix: Return a flag from the revive_failed branch. In both events, skip confirmShopPayment for metadata.shop_order_id when the late-payment refund succeeded, and name the bundled order in the ops mail. Alternative: refund only amount − bundled shop total (pass amount to refunds.create) and keep confirming the order.

issues.problem: An open stored PaymentIntent with the same attempt_id is returned ('reuse') without checking pi.amount === chargeCents, currency, metadata.type, chg_hash or due/card_rounding. The scratch test (same attempt, request 3000 Kč vs stored 1500 Kč) shows reuse. On the saved-card path the client would then confirm the old amount, so 'never charged other than sent' depends on clients never reusing an attempt_id for a changed request. The current app always generates a new id, so this is latent hardening.
issues.fix: Apply the same conditions as the sheet-reuse branch (amount, czk, md.type, chg_hash, metaOk) to the attempt-id reuse. If they do not match, fall through to cancel and create.

issues.problem:
1) The 'round' kind accepts any amount where Math.round(amount) === 15 (14.50–15.49), but charges Math.round(amount*100) while recording r = 15 − due. Example: card_min, due 7, amount 14.6 → 14.60 Kč charged, documents and total 15 Kč.
2) Carried over from f3 and still open: the ±1 Kč tolerance. Booking accepts round(amt) = round(due) ± 1, app-format/web edits accept |amount − expected| ≤ 1, and the web edit Checkout line uses the client amount. The difference is only recorded when |sub| < 1, so a tampered client is charged up to 1 Kč more or less than documented.
issues.fix: For kind 'round', set amountCents = CARD_MIN_CZK*100 (or refuse 400 unless Number(amount) === 15). Record the haléř difference when |sub| ≤ 1, or refuse amount_mismatch unless round(amount) === round(due) (upsell aside). For web edit Checkout, build the line item from extDue, not the client amount.

issues.problem: Carried over from f3, still open. `amountCzk = booking.total_price || body.amount || 0` uses the anonymous client amount when the DB total is 0. Since D1 this also drives the rounding path: floorCheck runs on the client 'due', a 1–15 Kč amount is charged 15, and the documents stay at 0 Kč (applyChargeRounding only logs a mismatch).
issues.fix: When the row was loaded, use only Number(booking.total_price) || 0 (0 = free/setup path). Fall back to body.amount only when the row has no total_price column.

issues.problem: Carried over from f3, still open (pre-existing). Booking and SOS payments are confirmed without comparing amount_received with total_price. The customer can lower total_price on an unpaid booking via RLS: the PP floor check only logs (PP_FLOOR_ENFORCE unset), and a PaymentIntent created earlier for a lower amount can still be paid. The booking ends 'paid' while the final invoice shows money owed.
issues.fix: After applyChargeRounding, compare amount_received/100 (minus the bundled shop total) with total_price. If it is short by more than 1 Kč (or the currency is not CZK), write debug_log 'booking_underpaid' and send the ops mail without blocking the confirmation. Turn on PP_FLOOR_ENFORCE=1 once the booking_price_below_floor calibration log is clean.

issues.problem: Carried over from f2, still open. A web swap with 0 < net ≤ 0.5 Kč still bypasses process-payment and commits directly as the customer (p_settle_refund). total_price rises by the net with no card_rounding −net, so the final invoice asks the customer for haléře. That breaks D1, which waives ≤ 1 Kč with a record. The app and the other web edit flows already use net > 0.
issues.fix: When MG.cardRoundingIsLive() is true, send every net > 0 through process-payment, where the server waives ≤ 1 Kč and redirects with waived=1, which paid.js already handles. Keep the 0.5 threshold until then.

issues.problem:
This predates the D1–D6 work ('vouchers to 0'):
- The web booking checkout has no voucher_unavailable check, unlike app payments (voucherProblem).
- The free path accepts a voucher_id whose amount covers the price regardless of vouchers.status/booking_id.
A voucher already redeemed by another booking can therefore still confirm a free (or discounted) web booking. redeem_booking_discounts_on_paid then silently no-ops, so one voucher is spent twice.
issues.fix: Call voucherProblem(supabaseAdmin, booking_id) in handleWebBookingCheckout before the waiver/free/payment branches: 409 voucher_unavailable with a web text. In both free paths, also require the voucher_id voucher to be 'active' or redeemed for this booking.

In the stored-id fallback, skip confirmBookingPayment and the card-brand update when the matched booking's payment_status is not 'unpaid'; log 'pi_fallback_skipped'. The session event already handles the surcharge.

issues.problem: With SQL p1 live, the server records the haléř difference of an app-format edit (sub = charge − due, e.g. +0.50). The app's expected total adds only cc.rounding, which is 0 for the 'normal' kind. When the due ends in exactly ,50 Kč, pollBookingTotal (tolerance < 0.5) never matches, so resume recovery and verify treat a paid edit as unconfirmed. For 4.1.3 the same mismatch triggers its client-side apply, which overwrites total_price without the +0.50. The final invoice then issues a 0.50 Kč overpay credit note.
issues.fix: App (both trees): expectedTotal = t + (cc.charge − cc.due) when |cc.charge − cc.due| < 1 (normal kind), or use the tolerance ≤ 0.5. Server: record the sub-crown difference only for card_min requests (not for 4.1.3 app-format edits), so the old app's client write cannot drop it.
